lessons.title: Cardiac Arrest & Post-ROSC: CPR physiology, rhythms, drugs, EtCO₂
lessons.summary: เข้าใจเหตุผลของ high-quality CPR, shock timing, epinephrine, reversible causes, capnography และ post-ROSC care แทนการจำ algorithm อย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) CPR physiology
paragraphs: Chest compressions generate coronary/cerebral perfusion. Compression pauses rapidly reduce perfusion; minimizing interruptions is therefore central. Full recoil preserves venous return.

sections.title: 2) Shockable vs non-shockable
paragraphs: VF/pVT: defibrillation is causal therapy; shock rapidly and resume CPR. PEA/asystole: prioritize CPR, epinephrine and reversible causes.
bullets: Epinephrine adult 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 min

sections.title: 3) Airway & capnography
paragraphs: Advanced airway should not delay initial CPR/defibrillation. Continuous waveform capnography is recommended to confirm/monitor ETT in adult arrest and can help assess CPR quality/trends.
bullets: Abrupt sustained rise in EtCO₂ may suggest ROSC
Persistently low/decreasing EtCO₂ → reassess CPR quality and other causes, not a stand-alone termination rule

sections.title: 4) Post-ROSC priorities
paragraphs: Reassess oxygenation/ventilation, blood pressure/perfusion, 12-lead ECG, cause of arrest, temperature management and neurologic status. Avoid hyperoxia/hypoventilation extremes and treat shock.

key_points: Epinephrine ASAP in nonshockable pediatric arrest
quick_review: EtCO₂ trend can support CPR quality assessment

research_updates.title: Pediatric epinephrine timing
research_updates.takeaway: 2025 evidence update found observational data favoring earlier epinephrine for initial nonshockable pediatric arrest, while timing in shockable rhythms remains uncertain because defibrillation must remain the priority.

actions.label: เปิด Cardiac Arrest Algorithm

quiz.q: ใน VF/pVT priority คืออะไร?
quiz.explain: Rapid defibrillation is the priority for shockable arrest.

quiz.q: Continuous waveform capnography in adult arrest is useful mainly for?
quiz.explain: AHA recommends waveform capnography to confirm/monitor ETT and it can support CPR quality assessment.

lessons.title: Adult BLS/ALS 2025: High-Quality CPR to Reversible Causes
lessons.summary: แกนของ adult resuscitation: CPR quality, early defibrillation, correct drug timing, airway without interrupting compressions และ reversible causes.

sections.title: 1) CPR physiology
paragraphs: Coronary and cerebral perfusion depend on compression quality and minimizing pauses. Rate 100–120/min, adequate depth and recoil, compressor change about every 2 min.

sections.title: 2) Rhythm strategy
paragraphs: VF/pVT → defibrillation + CPR; PEA/asystole → CPR + epinephrine promptly + reversible causes. Rhythm checks should be brief.

sections.title: 3) Airway/ventilation
paragraphs: Avoid hyperventilation. Once advanced airway is placed, continuous compressions with adult ventilation about 10/min; waveform capnography helps confirm tube and trend CPR physiology.

sections.title: 4) Reversible causes
paragraphs: Hypovolemia, hypoxia, hydrogen ion/acidosis, hypo-/hyperkalemia, hypothermia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, pulmonary/coronary thrombosis.

lessons.title: Adult Symptomatic Bradycardia: Perfusion Before Rate
lessons.summary: Bradycardia ต้องรักษาเมื่อทำให้ perfusion ไม่พอ ไม่ใช่เพราะตัวเลข HR ต่ำอย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) Is the bradycardia causing compromise?
paragraphs: Look for hypotension, acutely altered mental status, signs of shock, ischemic chest discomfort or acute heart failure. Athletes and sleep states can have physiologic bradycardia.

sections.title: 2) Immediate approach
paragraphs: Airway/oxygen as indicated, monitor, IV access, 12-lead if it does not delay treatment. Search causes: ischemia, hypoxia, hyperkalemia, hypothermia, drugs/toxins, conduction disease.

sections.title: 3) Escalation
paragraphs: AHA 2025 adult algorithm includes atropine and escalation to transcutaneous pacing and/or chronotropic infusion when atropine is ineffective, with expert consultation and transvenous pacing consideration.

sections.title: 4) Pacing pearls
paragraphs: Electrical capture must be followed by mechanical capture: palpable pulse/arterial waveform and improved perfusion. Provide analgesia/sedation if time and hemodynamics permit.

prehospital_focus: Prepare pacing pads early in high-grade block
pitfalls: Delaying pacing in high-grade block with shock

lessons.title: Adult Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse: Stability, Width, Regularity
lessons.summary: แยก unstable vs stable ก่อน แล้วใช้ QRS width/regularity ช่วยเลือก pathway.

sections.title: 1) Is tachycardia the cause?
paragraphs: Sinus tachycardia is usually a response to fever, pain, hypovolemia, sepsis, hypoxia or PE. Treat the driver rather than suppressing an appropriate compensatory rate.

sections.title: 2) Unstable tachyarrhythmia
paragraphs: Hypotension, shock, altered mental status, ischemic chest discomfort or acute heart failure attributable to tachyarrhythmia → synchronized cardioversion pathway.

sections.title: 3) Narrow vs wide
paragraphs: Narrow regular rhythms include SVT; irregular narrow often AF/flutter with variable conduction. Wide complex should be treated cautiously; VT is common and irregular wide raises concern for pre-excited AF or polymorphic VT.

sections.title: 4) Adenosine limits
paragraphs: Adenosine is useful in selected regular narrow-complex tachycardia and may be considered diagnostically/therapeutically in regular monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia per algorithm; avoid reflex use in irregular/polymorphic wide rhythms.

pitfalls: Using adenosine in irregular wide-complex rhythm

lessons.title: Post–Cardiac Arrest Care: Oxygen, Ventilation, Pressure, Temperature & Cause
lessons.summary: ROSC เป็นจุดเริ่มต้นของ phase ใหม่ที่ต้องป้องกัน secondary injury และหาสาเหตุ arrest.

sections.title: 1) Airway and gas exchange
paragraphs: Avoid both hypoxemia and unnecessary hyperoxia; use controlled oxygen when reliable saturation is available. Avoid marked hypo-/hypercapnia unless a specific clinical reason exists.

sections.title: 2) Hemodynamics
paragraphs: Post-arrest myocardial dysfunction and vasoplegia are common. Use repeated BP/perfusion assessment, fluids when appropriate and vasopressors for persistent hypotension.

sections.title: 3) ECG and coronary cause
paragraphs: Obtain 12-lead ECG and evaluate for coronary occlusion/ACS while considering noncoronary causes such as PE, hemorrhage, hypoxia and toxins.

sections.title: 4) Neurologic/temperature care
paragraphs: Prevent fever and use guideline-based temperature-control strategy in comatose survivors; avoid early definitive neurologic prognostication based on a single sign.

lessons.title: Capnography During CPR: What EtCO₂ Can and Cannot Tell You
lessons.summary: EtCO₂ เป็นทั้ง airway confirmation tool และ physiologic trend ระหว่าง CPR แต่ต้องตีความตาม ventilation, perfusion และ context.

sections.title: 1) Why EtCO₂ falls during arrest
paragraphs: CO₂ delivery to lungs is strongly influenced by pulmonary blood flow; during fixed ventilation, low EtCO₂ may reflect low cardiac output/poor CPR.

sections.title: 2) Use trends, not one number
paragraphs: Sudden sustained rise can accompany ROSC. Persistently low or falling values should prompt CPR-quality and airway/ventilation reassessment, not automatic termination by a single threshold.

sections.title: 3) Confounders
paragraphs: Ventilation rate/volume, bicarbonate, epinephrine, pulmonary embolism, severe lung disease and equipment issues alter EtCO₂.

sections.title: 4) Waveform matters
paragraphs: A waveform supports tracheal placement and ventilation continuity; loss of waveform demands immediate equipment/tube/patient reassessment.
